SAMPLE SIZE.evidence_source: A total of 115 students (63 male and 52 female, M age = 20.1 years) completed the MCSD, while a total of 184 students (94 males and 90 females, M age = 20.3) completed the WAIS–R tests.

ES.evidence_source: No correlation coefficient between intelligence scores (WAIS-R) and creative achievement (CAQ) was explicitly reported in the text. The correlation of '.91' is between WAIS-R subtests and the full-scale WAIS-R, not with creative achievement.

Effects.evidence_source: No effect sizes (correlation coefficients between intelligence and creative achievement) were found in the text.

Mage.evidence_source: A total of 115 students (63 male and 52 female, M age = 20.1 years) completed the MCSD, while a total of 184 students (94 males and 90 females, M age = 20.3) completed the WAIS–R tests.

Measure IQ.evidence_source: The 117 students from Study 1 were offered additional course credit to complete the MCSD and the Vocabulary and Block Design subtests of the Wechsler Adult Intelligence Test–Revised (WAIS–R; Wechsler, 1981).

IQ modality.evidence_source: The Vocabulary and Block Design subtests of the Wechsler Adult Intelligence Test–Revised (WAIS–R) were used. Vocabulary is verbal, and Block Design is figural, thus 'both' modalities are represented.

IQ Aspect.evidence_source: Previous research has shown that a composite score derived from these two subtests correlates .91 with the full-scale WAIS–R (Brooker & Cyr, 1986). Full-scale WAIS-R measures general intelligence (g).

Creativity Measures.evidence_source: All students had previously completed the CAQ.

Domain classified.evidence_source: The text does not specify a domain classification for creativity measures.

Number of studies.evidence_source: The 'Method' section describes the participants and procedure for a single study (referred to as Study X) that drew participants from previous studies (Study 1 and Study 3).

section_summary.extract_value: This section details the methodology for a study (referred to as Study X) involving participants drawn from previous Study 1 and Study 3. Participants completed the MCSD and the Vocabulary and Block Design subtests of the WAIS–R. The section provides sample sizes and mean ages for students who completed the MCSD (N=115, M age=20.1) and the WAIS–R tests (N=184, M age=20.3), noting that all students had previously completed the CAQ.
